question: Should OpenClaw expose `resetToken` on the shared harness-reset and plugin session-end payloads as the permanent discriminator for retained-session lifecycle cleanup?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive shared lifecycle contract, not a Codex-private implementation detail; the correct permanent discriminator and its ownership need maintainer intent beyond a contributor patch.

options.title: Approve the token contract after proof
options.body: Keep the two optional transient fields, provided exact-head runtime evidence and focused lifecycle tests demonstrate their intended ownership and fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Use a lifecycle-owned discriminator
options.body: Replace the transient shared token with a lifecycle value owned by the reset state model if maintainers want retry or cross-process semantics outside one runtime.

options.title: Pause for owner design
options.body: Hold the PR if neither contract has a clear long-term owner or compatibility story.

recommendation.title: Approve the token contract after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the two optional transient fields, provided exact-head runtime evidence and focused lifecycle tests demonstrate their intended ownership and fail-closed behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the retained-session reset model that creates the same-ID lifecycle boundary this contract must represent.
